samples.summary: Backend block-style alignment enum validation is scope creep beyond issue #728 and contradicts the PR's own stated rule that sink normalization, not API validation, is the fix
samples.evidence: Issue #728 (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md) is about the font-color reset painting the selection color; its acceptance criterion is purely about reset producing default ink. The new `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` / `assertValidBlockStyle` adds a new API contract (400 on unknown alignment) unrelated to color, and the PR's own lessons file (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:30-38) states "Normalizing at a sink covers every writer; validating at one API does not" — the exporter clamp `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` already fails closed, making the API check redundant belt-and-braces. It also newly rejects PUT bodies (e.g. GET→PUT round-trip of a document that somehow carries an unlisted alignment) that previously succeeded, and the new contract is not recorded in docs/design/rest-api.md.

samples.summary: The new alignment validation is applied only to the docs body arm; the slides arm accepts the same block styles unchecked, so the stated rationale is only half-realized
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is called from `assertValidBlock`, reachable only via `assertValidDocsBody`. `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidSlide`/`assertValidElement` (lines 343-435) never descend into text-element `TextBody.blocks`, so a slides PUT can still persist an arbitrary `style.alignment` into the CRDT — the very thing the comment at line 261-264 says is being prevented ("keeps the garbage out of the document in the first place"). Either the guard belongs at the shared sink only, or it should cover both arms.

samples.summary: The set of legal block alignments is now spelled out in three unrelated places with no shared source of truth
samples.evidence: `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` (backend controller:254), `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:104-109) and `ALGN` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79) each independently encode `left|center|right|justify`, while the canonical definition is the union type at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:103. The backend already imports docs types via packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.types.ts:19, so a single exported constant (docs model or @wafflebase/core) would keep them from drifting — the repo's stated reuse expectation.

samples.summary: `isEmptyStoredColor` widens the #728 "empty means unset" rule to any whitespace-only color, which is broader than the issue describes and is not documented anywhere
samples.evidence: The issue and both task docs describe exactly two shapes: the bare `''` written by the old reset, and `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }`. `c.trim() === ''` additionally treats `'   '` / `{ value: '  ' }` as unset. Harmless in practice but an undocumented behavior expansion at a shared helper used by every paint path (paint-layout.ts, table-renderer.ts, resolveColorAtPosition).

finding.summary: New OOXML export color policy is not recorded in any design doc (CONTRIBUTING requires updating the canonical subsystem doc for non-trivial changes)
finding.evidence: The diff changes documented export mappings — `docs-docx-import-export.md:299-312` still states the plain `<w:color w:val>` / `<w:shd w:fill>` ↔ `style.color`/`backgroundColor` correspondence, and `slides-pptx-export.md:148-151` still documents `{kind:'srgb'} → <a:srgbClr val="RRGGBB">` unconditionally, with no mention of the new rules introduced here (non-hex values drop the attribute/child, fully transparent colors drop, partial alpha renders opaque, `''` means unset). No `docs/design/**` file is touched by the diff; the only written record is the task plan `docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md`, which CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16,56-58 treats as the plan, not the design record. If reviewers consider this a bugfix only, no doc is owed; if the new shared model-level normalizer and export drop-policy count as a data-model/export contract change, the canonical docs should be updated rather than left stale.
